summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sonjaidee, director of the Joint Information Centre, stated that Thailand will strictly follow the December 27, 2025 joint statement: 'whoever is where must stay there.' This comes in response to Cambodian PM Hun Manet’s suggestion of talks after Songkran to reclaim territory. Prapas warned against distorted information and noted that any formal boundary discussions must wait for the new Thai government and go through the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).

summary: The Thai government has successfully distributed 3,313 million baht in compensation to 695,945 households across seven provinces bordering Cambodia. Sisaket and Surin saw the highest payouts. This aid follows cabinet resolutions from late 2025 to help civilians affected by the border conflict. Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely to ensure residents' safety.

summaryTh: รัฐบาลโอนเงินเยียวยาให้ประชาชนใน 7 จังหวัดชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ครบ 695,945 ครัวเรือนแล้ว รวมเป็นเงินกว่า 3,313 ล้านบาท โดยจังหวัดศรีสะเกษและสุรินทร์มียอดการโอนสูงสุด การช่วยเหลือนี้เป็นไปตามมติ ครม. เมื่อปลายปี 2568 เพื่อบรรเทาความเดือดร้อนของชาวบ้านที่ได้รับผลกระทบจากสถานการณ์ความขัดแย้งชายแดน

summary: Analysis highlights that while the border ceasefire has held for two months, it remains extremely fragile. The incoming government led by Anutin Charnvirakul, expected to take power after Parliament opens on March 14, will face immediate pressure to manage nationalistic sentiments and address border security. Experts warn that any inflammatory rhetoric on social media could reignite armed clashes.
summaryKh: ការវិភាគបានបង្ហាញថា ទោះបីជាបទឈប់បាញ់តាមព្រំដែនបានបន្តអស់រយៈពេល 2 ខែក៏ដោយ ប៉ុន្តែវានៅតែមានភាពផុយស្រួយបំផុត។ រដ្ឋាភិបាលថ្មីដែលដឹកនាំដោយលោក អនុទិន ឆានវីរៈកុល ដែលរំពឹងថានឹងឡើងកាន់អំណាចបន្ទាប់ពីការបើកសភាថ្ងៃទី 14 ខែមីនា នឹងប្រឈមមុខនឹងសម្ពាធភ្លាមៗក្នុងការគ្រប់គ្រងអារម្មណ៍ជាតិនិយម និងសន្តិសុខព្រំដែន។ អ្នកជំនាញព្រមានថា ការប្រើសម្តីបង្កហេតុតាមបណ្តាញសង្គមអាចធ្វើឱ្យមានការផ្ទុះអាវុធឡើងវិញ។
summaryTh: บทวิเคราะห์ระบุว่าแม้ข้อตกลงหยุดยิงจะดำเนินมาได้ 2 เดือนแล้ว แต่สถานการณ์ยังคงเปราะบางอย่างยิ่ง รัฐบาลใหม่ภายใต้การนำของนายอนุทิน ชาญวีรกูล ที่คาดว่าจะเข้ามารับหน้าที่หลังเปิดสภาในวันที่ 14 มีนาคม จะต้องเผชิญกับแรงกดดันในการจัดการกับกระแสชาตินิยมและความมั่นคงชายแดน นักวิชาการเตือนว่าวาทกรรมที่รุนแรงในโซเชียลมีเดียอาจจุดฉนวนให้เกิดการปะทะด้วยอาวุธขึ้นอีกครั้ง

summary: Major General Winthai Suvaree, Army spokesperson, stated that recent troop changes are routine rotations. He mentioned a specific incident on March 8, 2026, at Chong Samtae (Si Sa Ket), where Thai troops fired warning shots into the air after Cambodian soldiers approached a barbed-wire fence and engaged in provocative behavior. The Army remains on alert but believes military escalation is unlikely as Cambodia lacks a military advantage.
summaryKh: ឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ទោ Winthai Suvaree អ្នកនាំពាក្យកងទ័ពបានបញ្ជាក់ថា ការផ្លាស់ប្តូរកម្លាំងទ័ពនាពេលថ្មីៗនេះ គឺជាការផ្លាស់ប្តូរតាមវេនធម្មតា។ លោកបានលើកឡើងពីព្រឹត្តិការណ៍ជាក់លាក់មួយនៅថ្ងៃទី 8 ខែមីនា ឆ្នាំ 2026 នៅតំបន់ច្រកសំទែរ (ខេត្តស៊ីសាកេត) ដែលកងទ័ពថៃបានបាញ់កាំភ្លើងគំរាមឡើងលើ បន្ទាប់ពីទាហានកម្ពុជាចូលមកជិតរបងលួសបន្លានិងមានសកម្មភាពឌឺដង។ កងទ័ពនៅតែបន្តតាមដាន ប៉ុន្តែជឿថានឹងមិនមានការប៉ះទង្គិចធំដុំទេ ព្រោះកម្ពុជាមិនទាន់មានប្រៀបផ្នែកយោធា។

summary: Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, Army spokesperson, stated that the border situation is under control. He reported that at Chong Sam Tae in Si Sa Ket, new Cambodian soldiers have been seen filming 'provocative content' near Thai fences. summary: Thai rangers at the Aranyaprathet border arrested nine Thai nationals (4 men, 5 women) who were found crawling through razor wire from Poipet back into Thailand. They escaped during a Cambodian crackdown, hiding in temples before crossing. No travel documents were found on them.

Thailand alleges these centers were used as military bases and weapons storage by Cambodian forces. Approximately 20,000 workers reportedly fled before the Thai strikes.

summary: The Royal Thai Armed Forces will begin constructing a permanent 1.3km border fence in Pong Nam Ron district, Chanthaburi, starting in April 2026. The pilot project aims to deter illegal trade and transnational crime. The military emphasized that this is a security measure for residents and is being coordinated with Cambodian authorities, featuring high-tech surveillance like motion sensors and CCTV.

summary: Phnom Penh has filed a formal diplomatic protest against the Thai military for building infrastructure, including roads, stairs, and Buddha statues, near the Preah Vihear and Ta Krabei temples. Cambodia claims these actions violate the 2000 MoU by altering the physical landscape of contested areas. This follows a period of intense border clashes late last year that resulted in high casualties and closed borders.

summary: Activist Panthep Puapongpan shared historical records arguing that the Thailand-Cambodia border at Preah Vihear should be demarcated by the 'cliff edge' (watershed line) as intended by Thai ancestors. He argues that following this principle would protect Thai sovereignty over overlapping areas. This comes amid high domestic pressure on the Thai government regarding border negotiations and the revocation of MoU 44.

summary: The Thai military organized a tour for international media at an abandoned scam compound in the Chong Chom border area of Surin province. Journalists saw scattered documents containing personal data of Japanese citizens and rooms set up to look like foreign police stations. The military reports that around 20,000 workers fled the site just before it was hit by artillery during recent border clashes.

summary: Air Marshal Prapas Sornchaidee, Director of the Situation Information Center, addressed concerns over border tensions, stating the situation is under control. He advised monitoring military movements, weapons logistics, and political signals to evaluate risks. He emphasized reducing provocation and maintaining direct communication to prevent localized issues from escalating into major conflicts.

summary: Thai military officials escorted journalists to an 800,000-square-meter compound in Chong Chom, Surin, which served as a massive scam hub. The facility was abandoned recently following heavy artillery fire in the area. Evidence found inside included fake police uniforms from various countries, torture equipment, and personal data of Japanese citizens. The base reportedly housed up to 20,000 workers before the recent military escalation forced a mass evacuation.

summary: Thai and Cambodian authorities have activated the Joint Information Center (JIC) mechanism to handle a viral edited image of Cambodian Senate President Hun Sen's face superimposed on tree roots (mimicking a famous Buddha head image). summary: The Thai Mine Action Center (TMAC) reported significant progress in demining operations at Ban Dan, Surin province. As of March 17, over 300 landmines have been cleared. While 34.16% of the target area in Sector 1 has been declared safe, officials warn that over 65% of the zone remains at risk. This operation is part of ongoing efforts to secure border areas following past conflicts.

summary: Cambodia is increasing fuel imports from Singapore and Malaysia due to supply cuts from Vietnam and China. Trade in energy and petroleum products between Thailand and Cambodia has remained completely suspended since the armed conflict began in July 2024. Previously, Thailand and Vietnam accounted for over 60% of Cambodia's annual fuel imports.

summary: The Royal Thai Army has formally dismissed Cambodia's protest which accused Thai troops of violating sovereignty. Spokesman Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree stated that all military activities, including construction and land-clearing near areas like Preah Vihear and Ta Muen Thom, are conducted within Thai territory and comply with the December 27 ceasefire. He noted that such actions are necessary for security monitoring following recent clashes.

summary: The Army spokesperson confirmed that the situation at the border near Ta Kwai Temple in Surin province is currently stable. Intelligence reports suggest that recent Cambodian troop movements may be related to their internal politics rather than an immediate plan to attack. Thai forces remain strictly committed to the ceasefire agreement but are ready to respond immediately to any sovereignty violations.

summary: Lt. Gen. Theeranan Nanthakwang, Chief of Army Intelligence, warned that a third round of clashes with Cambodia is likely. He cited two major indicators: Cambodia's large-scale purchase of weapons from Eastern Europe and its upcoming 2027 elections. He urged Thai troops to remain vigilant and use lessons from previous battles to improve readiness, specifically highlighting the window 4-5 months from now after the rainy season.

summary: A Thai Senate ad hoc committee has recommended the cancellation of the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 43) on border demarcation. Senator Nophadol Inna stated the agreement is flawed, specifically regarding the use of Cambodian maps that conflict with Thai records. The committee argues the pact has failed to resolve disputes over 26 years and that Cambodia continues to provoke Thai forces by laying mines.

summary: A Senate extraordinary committee chaired by Nopadol Inna has voted unanimously to urge the Thai government to cancel the MOU 2000 border agreement. The committee argues the agreement is unconstitutional as it never received proper parliamentary approval and relies on a 1:200,000 scale map that favors Cambodia. The move follows two major military clashes in 2025 and a previous recommendation to cancel the maritime MOU 2001 (MOU 44).

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the border situation is normal following reports of military movements. He explained that these were routine troop rotations and told citizens not to worry, as the military is prepared but not anticipating new clashes. This statement aims to calm public concerns after rumors of a potential new conflict began spreading on social media.

summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul downplayed reports of Cambodian troop movements near the border. summary: Cambodia has warned Thailand that unilaterally canceling the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on land boundaries would be a violation of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. Cambodian officials argue that the agreement is essential for peaceful dispute resolution and that the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) has already made progress in marking 74 border points. This comes as a response to growing calls within the Thai Senate to scrap the pact.

summaryTh: กัมพูชาได้ส่งสัญญาณเตือนไทยว่า การยกเลิกบันทึกความเข้าใจ (MOU) ปี 2543 เกี่ยวกับเขตแดนทางบกเพียงฝ่ายเดียว ถือเป็นการละเมิดอนุสัญญาเวียนนาว่าด้วยกฎหมายสนธิสัญญา ทางการกัมพูชาแย้งว่าข้อตกลงนี้จำเป็นต่อการแก้ปัญหาอย่างสันติ และที่ผ่านมาคณะกรรมาธิการเขตแดนร่วม (JBC) ได้มีความคืบหน้าในการปักปันหลักเขตแดนไปแล้ว 74 จุด การเคลื่อนไหวนี้มีขึ้นหลังจากที่มีกระแสเรียกร้องจากคณะกรรมาธิการของวุฒิสภาไทยให้ยกเลิกข้อตกลงดังกล่าว

Authorities have already seized several shipments and are maintaining a strict watch to prevent further incursions.

summary: Phnom Penh has officially dismissed a recommendation from a Thai Senate committee to revoke the 2000 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 2000) regarding land boundaries. Cambodian officials labeled the move as 'politically motivated' and warned that dismantling this legal framework could lead to a military confrontation. This follows a unanimous vote by a Thai Senate panel on March 24 to scrap the pact, citing concerns over sovereignty and mapping.

summary: Business sectors are urging the new Anutin 2 government to reverse the hardline approach that caused nearly 1 million Cambodian workers to flee Thailand since mid-2025. The editorial argues that the ban on Cambodian labor hurts Thai businesses and encourages illegal crossings, suggesting that economic security is just as vital as border security.

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) has rejected allegations from Phnom Penh that Thai troops are preventing tens of thousands of displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes.
